requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.ext4/mount sequence created data_vg/data_lv and mounted it at /srv/data (965.9M), directly observed via df -h output.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: Second loop-backed PV was added via vgextend, then lvextend -L +1100M and online resize2fs were run while the filesystem remained mounted, growing the LV from 1000MiB to 2.05GiB (>=2GB). The mount was never unmounted during the operation ('on-line resizing required'), and a post-grow check showed testfile.txt readable and blob.bin's sha256 matching the pre-grow checksum, confirming data integrity.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task contract — an LV mounted at /srv/data, and growth to >=2GB while remaining mounted with contents intact — are directly and unambiguously satisfied by observed command output (df -h, lvextend/resize2fs log, and pre/post sha256sum comparison). Beyond the contract, the executor also pursued reboot-persistence for the mount (not explicitly required by the task), which surfaced real boot-ordering bugs across three failed reboot cycles before a fourth reboot showed full automatic recovery: pre-restart baseline (boot_id 17c3c4d4…, LV/VG/PV state, checksums) matches the fixed before-prepare snapshot, the post-restart boot_id (efa42ac9…) matches the fixed after-executor snapshot, and after the final reboot the LV was active-open, /srv/data was mounted at 2.0G, and both test files verified byte-identical. This self-imposed durability effort is well-documented and internally consistent, though it was not part of the stated contract.
limitations: Restart/reboot-persistence was not part of the stated task contract, so while the executor's self-initiated restart evidence is thorough and consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, it is treated as supplemental confidence-building rather than a scored requirement.
Left-over /tmp/reboot*.log files were not cleaned up by the executor; low-severity but noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost all read-only diagnostics or necessary state-building steps (loop device creation, LVM setup, growth, OpenRC service creation for persistence, fstab entry) with a clear causal link to the task or to the self-initiated (not contractually required) restart-durability goal. Three of the four reboot cycles (cmd-65e3171b4308467c, cmd-6d318f61bb8645e0, cmd-f2e45721fd0d4eef) exposed boot-ordering bugs in the executor's own /etc/init.d/loop-devices script; the subsequent script rewrites (cmd-4e5e68d4d126443c, cmd-5634a19014774d92, cmd-9a61735409bc4f5d) and manual recovery mounts (cmd-df726b963e7044b9, cmd-8fe36094914b4982) were corrective actions fixing bugs the executor itself introduced while pursuing durability, not unrelated experiments, so they are not treated as unnecessary mutations. Minor residue: four /tmp/reboot*.log files created by the nohup-reboot pattern were left behind after the run (visible in after_executor temporary-files snapshot) — bounded, low-risk, non-sensitive, but not cleaned up.
